what: Tolkien Gateway's external-citation graph joined to what this archive holds. Every external-link use in the wiki's main namespace, collapsed to works and to hosts, and matched against arda_scholarship.json and arda_mss_catalogue.json on a published normalisation. It answers section III.4 -- which works the field leans on and how heavily -- and feeds section I.6, which asks the archive to tell an independent source from a derivative one.
rule: A CITATION COUNT IS NOT AUTHORITY. Section IV: do not assign canon merely because a fact appears in Tolkien Gateway. TOLKIEN GATEWAY IS t4 and nothing in this file is a tier or may raise one; every row carries conf EXT and no row carries a tier. What is published here is STANDING -- how much attention one wiki pays a work -- and standing is a fact about the wiki, not about Arda and not about whether the work is right.
repetition_is_not_confirmation: Section I.5. Many Gateway articles citing one work is ONE SOURCE CITED MANY TIMES, not many witnesses. A high `gateway_uses` means the wiki returns to a work often; it is not corroboration, and two wiki articles agreeing are not two witnesses because they share editors, templates and each other. The graph's own loudest row makes the point better than the rule does: the most prolific citing article in it is a collectible-card list, and its citations are one vendor database repeated.
not_republished: METADATA AND LINK STRUCTURE ONLY. No wiki article text is carried here -- a row holds a page id, a page title and an external URL. The wiki's prose was discarded at the crawl and is not in this file.
no_tier: No row carries a tier, because a citation count is not a claim about Arda. It is a claim about Tolkien Gateway, checkable against the API capture named in `provenance`, and the URL is its own citation.

provenance.discovery_path: research/registry/sources.jsonl seed list owner-2026-08-26 -> MediaWiki api.php
provenance.stage: /home/raz/.arda-crawl-stage/gap-20260826 -- READ, NEVER COMMITTED. Only this derived join is published.
provenance.revision_ids: NOT AVAILABLE ON THIS AXIS, AND NOT INVENTED. MediaWiki's list=exturlusage returns pageid, ns, title and url and no revision id, so no row here can carry one. What anchors the capture instead is the sha256 and the retrieval timestamp above, both of which are checkable, plus the stable pageid on every citing article. The same crawl's Index: and Portal: capture DOES carry revision ids and the number of them is in `counts`.

normalisation.why: The corpus and these titles are mixed-normalisation, so a raw comparison misses -- `Lothlorien` against `Loth-\nlorien` is a real miss, not a theory. The key is PUBLISHED so a reader can reproduce it rather than trust it.
url_key: NFKD, then drop every combining mark (accents fold)
drop U+00AD soft hyphen; join `-\n`; drop newlines and carriage returns
lowercase the host; drop any userinfo and any port
drop trailing slashes from the path
drop utm_*, fbclid and gclid parameters; sort the rest

bepress_key.rule: `cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=N&context=C` and `/context/C/article/N/` both become `bepress:HOST/C/N`; the archive's OAI identifier `oai:HOST:C-N` becomes the same string.
bepress_key.why: The wiki links Digital Commons PDFs by article number while the archive holds the landing page. Without this key the two never meet.
bepress_key.proof: NOT ASSUMED. Every held PDF that carries BOTH an OAI identifier and a viewcontent-style PDF URL is one test of the identity; the counts that agree and disagree are in counts.bepress_key_proof, and the first twenty disagreements would be listed in `bepress_key_disagreements` if there were any.

marquette_family_key.rule: for marquette.edu, take the leaf of a path under `/archives/Mss/JRRT/`, drop its extension, lowercase it, and drop a leading `jrrt-` or `mss-`.
marquette_family_key.why: The wiki links the same finding-aid page under three spellings the site has used over the years -- `.shtml`, `.php` and a `/collections/` path -- while the mss catalogue carries only the current one. Comparing raw URLs calls three spellings three pages.
marquette_family_key.what_it_does_not_do: It does not fold `mss-jrrt-s-5.html` onto `JRRT-series5.php`. That fold would need a hand-written table of the site's old naming, and an honest miss is better than a hand-tuned match nobody can check.

normalisation.title_key: fold case, accents and hyphenation, strip markup tags, then remove every non-alphanumeric character. MEASURED AND REFUSED -- see `title_axis_refused`.

url_axis.what_was_sampled: THE WHOLE MATCHED POPULATION, not a sample of it. Every distinct (gateway_url, join_key) pair the join produced was read by hand against the archive record it reached.
url_axis.how_each_was_read: The bepress path segments carry volume, issue and article number, so a pair is right or wrong on its face; and two were checked a second way, against MEANING rather than string. Gateway's article `Imram` -- Tolkien's poem on St Brendan -- cites the Mythlore paper `Sailing West: Tolkien, the Saint Brendan Story, and the Idea of Paradise`. Gateway's articles `Tolkien Gateway` and `Janet Brennan Croft` both cite Croft's `Bibliographic Resources for Literature Searches on J.R.R Tolkien`. Subject agreement, not just path agreement.
the_four_marquette_folds_named_one_by_on: JRRT-hunnewell.shtml and JRRT-hunnewell.php -> the archive's JRRT-hunnewell.php
JRRT-series7.shtml and JRRT-series7.php -> the archive's JRRT-series7.php
url_axis.what_would_make_this_wrong: a normalisation step that folded two DIFFERENT resources together. Three candidates were checked on the pairs where they actually fired: the tracking-parameter strip (2 pairs, both bepress cover-page parameters on an otherwise identical path), the trailing-slash strip, and the Marquette family fold (4 keys, named above). None changed which resource was denoted. A URL matched by BOTH url_key and marquette_family_key appears twice on purpose, one row per key, so the file records which key reached it -- which is why `join_rows` exceeds `join_distinct_gateway_urls_matched`.

title_axis.what_was_sampled: THE WHOLE POPULATION OF DISTINCT PAIRS the title key produced, read one by one against what each side denotes. Each verdict carries the reading that decided it in the generator's TITLE_SAMPLE_VERDICTS table, so the rate can be argued with rather than believed.
title_axis.criterion: `same_work` is true only where the archive row and the wiki article denote the SAME BIBLIOGRAPHIC WORK. A manuscript OF a book against the article ABOUT that book counts. A folder of somebody's letters against the article about that person does not, because a person is not a work.

title_axis_refused.verdict: REFUSED. The title key is not published as a join for these two datasets and no row of this file rests on it.
title_axis_refused.why: A scholarship title names an ARTICLE ABOUT Tolkien and a wiki title names a THING IN ARDA, so an agreement between them is usually coincidence: a Mythic Circle poem called `The Eye` is not the wiki's article on Sauron's Eye. A manuscript title names a FOLDER and a wiki title names a PERSON or a BOOK, so `John Ronald Reuel Tolkien` matches a box of paper against a biography. The strings agree and the referents do not, which is the one fault a normalisation cannot fix by getting better.
title_axis_refused.kept_anyway: the key and the measured rate stay in this file because a refusal that cannot be reproduced is an opinion. A later session that wants this axis can rerun it and argue with the readings.

what_the_graph_shows_about_its_own_measu: THE SECOND-MOST-CITED HOST IS eldamo.org -- Paul Strack's lexicon -- and the archive already publishes that project's data as site/arda_eldamo_lexicon.json. The wiki leans on it hard and the archive holds it: an agreement between two independent judgements about what matters, which is worth more than either.

THE MOST PROLIFIC CITING ARTICLE IN THE GRAPH CITES ONE VENDOR DATABASE. gatherer.wizards.com carries 643 distinct URLs across TWO articles, and brickset.com 271 across ONE. Ranked by `gateway_uses` alone those hosts sit among the most-cited in Tolkien scholarship, and they are a card list and a Lego catalogue. This is section I.5 in one row: repetition is not confirmation, and a count of uses without a count of CITING ARTICLES beside it is a number that lies. Both are on every host row for exactly this reason.
A HOST'S RANK HERE IS NOT ITS STANDING IN THE FIELD, it is its standing ON ONE WIKI. imdb.com outranks every scholarly publisher in the graph.
how_to_read_it: `standing_by_host` ranks every host in the wiki's citation graph by uses, with arda_domain_graph.json's class beside it where that file knows the host. `join` is the matched rows: a Gateway URL, the articles that cite it, and the archive record it reaches. `cited_not_held` is direction two of the missing-data finding, narrowed to scholarly hosts so the rows can be acted on; its denominator is in counts.cited_but_not_held. Direction one -- what the archive holds and the wiki never cites -- is a COUNT with its population beside it in counts.held_but_never_cited, not a list, because the list is every row of two published datasets minus a hundred-odd and is derivable from them.
relation_to_arda_domain_graph: arda_domain_graph.json already answers section I.6 from what the ARCHIVE holds. This file adds what ONE WIKI cites, which is a different population and a weaker kind of evidence. The two are joined by host and NOT merged: the class on a host row here is read out of that file, never re-decided, and this generator writes nothing into it.

counts.join_rows_what: one row per (Gateway URL, join key, archive dataset). The archive rows a row reaches are counted in `archive_rows_reached`, not exploded into separate rows -- one Marquette finding-aid page carries hundreds of catalogue rows and exploding them reads as hundreds of independent matches when it is one link.
counts.hosts_the_archive_also_holds_a_url_on_de: measured against the URL index of arda_scholarship.json and arda_mss_catalogue.json ONLY, which is the whole population this join covers. IT IS NOT A CENSUS OF WHAT THE ARCHIVE HOLDS: eldamo.org reads false here while site/arda_eldamo_lexicon.json is 11.3 MB of that project's data, because the lexicon carries no URL of its own for a key to reach. A proxy is not the property.
